title: IPC-A-610 Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies
section: §10 through-hole solder fill — vertical barrel fill minimums by class (75 % for Class 2 and Class 3)
verifiedBy: READ. Primary IPC-A-610D fragments read: "Class 2, fill to 75% but with exception for inner layer connections" and "All other solder joints remain according to IPC-A-610 Class 2". Settled the round-10 contradiction — 75 % is the minimum for both classes; the 50 % figure belongs to IPC-6012 Rev F (bare board).

title: J-STD-001 Requirements for Soldered Electrical and Electronic Assemblies
section: §8 cleanliness — objective evidence in place of the single ROSE limit
verifiedBy: READ. Amendment 1 to Rev G (2018) and Rev H (September 2020) confirmed from IPC's own site and three independent reproductions: the 1.56 µg/cm² ROSE pass/fail was removed and replaced by objective evidence — SIR per IPC-TM-650 2.6.3.7, ion chromatography per 2.3.28, temperature-humidity-bias, or documented field history.

title: J-STD-033 Handling, Packing, Shipping and Use of Moisture, Heat and ESD Sensitive Surface Mount Devices
section: Table 4-1 (user bake) and Table 4-2 (supplier dry-pack); Table 5-1 floor life; §4.2.7.1 cumulative bake
verifiedBy: READ. Primary J-STD-033B.1 and Rev D text read. The full Table 4-1 matrix was recovered — thickness × MSL level × whether floor life was exceeded by more or less than 72 h. Table 4-2 is the supplier dry-pack bake at a fixed 24 h maximum exposure. Cumulative bake above 90 °C and up to 125 °C limited to 96 h; at 90 °C or below there is no limit.

title: IPC-7525C Stencil Design Guidelines (stencil design guidance: area ratio, aspect ratio, aperture sizing)
section: §1.1.2 area ratio; §1.1.3 aspect ratio
verifiedBy: READ. Primary IPC-7525B §1.1.2 and §1.1.3 read verbatim. Revision history confirmed independently: 7525 May 2000, A February 2007, B October 2011, C November 2021 (current). IPC-7525D does not exist. Caveat that still stands: the 0.66 and 1.5 FIGURES are carried only by convergent secondary sources and have not been confirmed against the standard body text.

title: J-STD-020 Classification of Moisture Sensitivity for Non-Hermetic Sealing Solid State Surface Mount Devices
edition: Rev D (read against Rev E text)
section: Table 4-1 and Table 4-2 classification temperatures; Table 5-2 classification reflow profile
verifiedBy: READ. Primary J-STD-020E text read. Table 4-2 (Pb-free) is thickness × volume: below 1.6 mm every volume 260 °C; 1.6-2.5 mm 260/250/245; above 2.5 mm 250/245/245. Table 4-1 (SnPb) 235 °C for thickness below 2.5 mm and volume below 350 mm³, 220 °C otherwise. Profile parameters: tL 60-150 s, ts 60-120 s, ramp-up 3 °C/s max, ramp-down 6 °C/s max, tp 20 s SnPb / 30 s Pb-free.

title: ISO 2859-1 Sampling procedures for inspection by attributes
section: Table I sample size code letters; Table II-A single sampling plans
verifiedBy: READ. A hosted copy of ISO 2859-1 itself was read, and the tables confirmed against three independent reproductions. Code letters A 2 through R 2000 (S 3150 omitted by the course); level II gives 501-1200 → J(80), 1201-3200 → K(125), 3201-10000 → L(200); at AQL 1.0 % K → Ac 3 / Re 4 and L → Ac 5 / Re 6.

title: IPC-7530 Guidelines for Temperature Profiling for Mass Soldering Processes
section: Reflow and wave profile guidance — ramp, soak, time above liquidus, cooling
verifiedBy: READ via the AIM Solder profile supplement, which reproduces the IPC/JEDEC classification profile table verbatim: time above liquidus 30-90 s, soak zone 150-200 °C, ramp up rate below 3 °C/sec with 1-3 °C/sec as the recommended starting point, cooling below 4 °C/sec. The IPC-7530A industry draft note that component suppliers often recommend a more conservative 2-4 °C/s was also read.

title: IPC-7711/7721 Rework, Modification and Repair of Electronic Assemblies
section: Rework and repair procedures; acceptable rework and repair methods
verifiedBy: READ from two independent renderings of the primary text. IPC-7711 is Rework, IPC-7721 is Repair and Modification, published together as IPC-7711/7721. IPC-7721 judges laminate repair on the restored condition — insulation and clearance maintained, no epoxy in the hole or on internal pad walls, no reduction in hole diameter, no exposed adjacent circuitry — and sets no damage depth limit. The only 0.25 mm in IPC-7721 is the width of a milled channel for a foil jumper.

title: IPC-CC-830 Qualification and Performance of Electrical Insulating Compound for Conformal Coating
section: §1.3.1 coating type designations; qualification and performance requirements
verifiedBy: READ from two independent renderings. Type AR acrylic, Type ER EPOXY, Type SR silicone, Type UR POLYURETHANE, Type XY PARAXYLYLENE, Type UT ultra-thin, Type SC styrene block co-polymer. There is no Type DR. The course had ER as polyurethane and invented DR for parylene.

title: IPC-TM-650 method 2.3.25 (ROSE) and 2.3.28 (ion chromatography)
section: Method 2.3.25 (ROSE, soluble ionic contamination) and method 2.3.28 (ion chromatography)
verifiedBy: READ. Method numbers and titles confirmed. 2.3.25 measures soluble ionic contamination as sodium chloride equivalent; 2.3.28 is ion chromatography, used to confirm the specific ions. Unit conversion cross-checked: 1.56 µg/cm² = 10.06 µg/in².

title: AIM Solder — Profile Supplement for Wave Soldering Process (flux deposition 500-1500 µg/in²)
section: Reflow and wave profile supplement — flux deposition, ramp, soak, time above liquidus, cooling
licenseNote: public vendor document; confirm current revision before publication
verifiedBy: READ. The AIM Solder supplement reproduces the IPC/JEDEC profile table and states flux deposition of 500-1500 µg/in² of flux solids, which converts to 0.775-2.325 g/m² — the course's 0.78-2.33 g/m² is exact. Also the source for the 30-90 s time-above-liquidus window.

title: J-STD-005 Requirements for Soldering Pastes (powder size distribution, Type 3 = 25-45 µm, 80% minimum in range)
section: Table 3-2 solder powder size distribution
verifiedBy: READ. The AIM Solder test report reproduces the standard's own Table 3-2 header and Type 3 row verbatim, confirmed independently by two further sources: none larger than 50 µm, less than 1 % larger than 45 µm, 80 % minimum between 25-45 µm, 10 % maximum smaller than 20 µm. Some older renderings of the table show a different layout, which is where the course's wrong tails came from.

title: IPC-A-600 Acceptability of Printed Boards (visual and dimensional criteria)
section: §2.10.3 annular ring; §3.5.3.1 conductor width reduction
verifiedBy: READ. IPC-A-600 §2.10.3: "Acceptable — Class 3: holes are not centered in the lands, but the annular ring measures 0.050 mm [0.0020 in] or more", with up to 20 % local reduction for pits, dents, nicks, pinholes or splay. §3.5.3.1: allowable reduction of the minimum conductor width due to misregistration or isolated defects shall not exceed 20 % of the minimum conductor width (10 % at Class 3).
